rule_evidence.statement: The script sets gblUserAuthorityLimit to the limit of the user's authority found in clm_HandlerAuthorities where the user's email matches. It also sets gblIsManager to true if the user's email is found in colManagers.Email. Finally, it collects a list of claim types ['Motor', 'Home', 'Theft', 'Injury', 'Travel'] into colClaimTypes.

The label 'lblSummaryResolution' is visible if the complaint is resolved to satisfaction and the difference in days between the complaint receipt date and the resolution date is 3 days or less. This condition decides whether the label should be displayed or not.

The label 'lblComplaintBreach' is hidden if the checkbox 'chkFinalResponseSent' is not checked and the difference in days between the 'dpComplaintReceived' date and the 'dpAsOf' date is greater than 56 days. This rule decides whether a complaint breach label should be visible or not.

The condition is whether ddComplaintOutcome.Selected.Value is 'Upheld' or 'Partially upheld'. If it is 'Upheld', the output is the sum of txtFinancialLoss.Text and an additional 150 if chkDistressInconvenience.Value is true. If it is 'Partially upheld', the output is half of txtFinancialLoss.Text rounded to two decimal places and an additional 75 if chkDistressInconvenience.Value is true. The effect is to set lblRedress.Text to the calculated value.

The condition is if either chkVulnerable.Value is true or ddChannel.Selected.Value is 'Regulator', then the label lblComplaintRoute.Text will be set to 'Escalated', otherwise it will be set to 'Standard'.
The policy number must be exactly 10 characters long and start with 'PL'. If the policy number is blank or does not meet these criteria, an error message is displayed.
The Incident date is outside the policy period if the selected Incident date is before the Policy Start date or after the Policy End date. Otherwise, no message is displayed.
The text in lblDateOrderError.Text will be set to 'Incident date cannot be after the notification date' if the selected incident date is later than the selected notification date.
The label 'lblLateNotification' is visible if the difference between the selected incident date and notified date is more than 30 days. This condition decides whether a notification is overdue.

The condition is if ddFault.Selected.Value is 'At fault', then the output is the maximum of 0 and the difference between the value of txtNcdYears.Text and 2, otherwise the value of txtNcdYears.Text. This rule determines the number of years of no claims discount based on fault status.

The button 'btnSubmit' is disabled if the policy number is blank, the incident date is blank, the claim amount is less than or equal to zero, or if there is a cover error message. Otherwise, the button is in edit mode.

locations.reason: data query: served by the list endpoint; filter/sort is a scenario-tested gap

rule_evidence.statement: The condition is that claims with status 'Referred' and assigned to the current user's email are sorted by the notification date in ascending order. The threshold values are 'Referred' for status and the current user's email for assigned to. The effect is sorting the items in the galReferrals.Items collection.
The condition is whether the selected claim type is 'Motor', 'Home', 'Theft', or 'Injury'. If not, the excess value is set to 500. The effect is setting the lblExcess.Text to the determined value.

The condition is if chkVatRegistered.Value is true, then set lblVatRecoverable.Text to the rounded value of lblNetSettlement.Text divided by 6, otherwise set it to 0. The threshold values are the value of lblNetSettlement.Text and 6. The effect is to set the text of lblVatRecoverable.Text.

If the selected claim type is 'Motor' and the vehicle age is greater than 5 years, then calculate the betterment amount as the cost of parts multiplied by a factor of 0.5 for the first 5 years and then by a decreasing factor of 0.1 for each additional year, rounding the result to 2 decimal places. Otherwise, set the betterment amount to 0.
UNINTERPRETED: lblSortCodeError.Text is set by the legacy logic at SettlementScreen/lblSortCodeError.Text.

The Late Interest label is set to the calculated interest amount if the difference between the agreed and paid dates is more than 14 days, otherwise it is set to 0. The interest amount is calculated as the net settlement amount multiplied by 8% and then by the number of days over 14, divided by 365, rounded to 2 decimal places.

The payment approval button displays as Edit mode if the claim amount is less than or equal to the user authority limit and there is no fraud referral label and no sort code error label. Otherwise, it displays as Disabled mode.

The authority level is determined based on the claim amount. If the claim amount is less than or equal to 5000, the handler is assigned. If the claim amount is between 5000 and 25000, the team leader is assigned. Otherwise, the claims manager is assigned.
The label 'lblFourEyes' is visible if the claim amount entered in 'txtClaimAmount' is greater than 10000. This rule decides whether the label should be shown or not based on the claim amount.

The condition checks if the incident date is within 30 days of the policy start date, if the number of prior claims is 3 or more, if the notified date is more than 30 days after the incident date, and if the 'No Police Ref' checkbox is checked and the claim type is 'Theft'. If any of these conditions are met, the fraud score is set to 40, 30, 20, or 10 respectively. Otherwise, the fraud score is set to 0.

The condition is that the value of lblFraudScore.Text must be greater than or equal to 50. If this condition is met, lblFraudReferral.Visible is set to true, allowing the referral label to be visible.
The label 'lblVulnerable' is visible if the user is 75 years or older than the date of notification, or if the preferred contact is 'Third party (Power of Attorney)'.

The priority label is set to 'P1' if the 'Vulnerable' label is visible, or if the selected claim type is 'Injury'. It is set to 'P2' if the claim amount is greater than 25000. Otherwise, it is set to 'P3'.
The SlaDays label is set to 2 days if the Priority label is 'P1', to 5 days if the Priority label is 'P2', and to 10 days otherwise. This rule determines the severity level of a claim.
The button 'btnAutoDecline' is disabled if either the 'lblVulnerable' label is visible or the 'lblFraudScore' text value is 50 or more. Otherwise, it is in edit mode.
The condition is that if the value of txtClaimAmount.Text is greater than 50000, then 'Apply 5% large-loss handling surcharge' will be displayed. Otherwise, nothing will be displayed.
